identity.title: Autocatalytic split-crRNA Cas12a circuit coupled with phosphorothioate G-quadruplex fluorescence for ultrasensitive ctDNA analysis.

content.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as an important biomarker for early cancer diagnosis and therapeutic monitoring; however, the ultrasensitive detection of low-abundance single-nucleotide variations (SNVs) remains highly challenging. Herein, we developed an autocatalytic split-crRNA Cas12a fluorescence platform, termed AutoSCas, for highly sensitive detection of EGFR L858R mutant ctDNA. Upon recognition of trace EGFR L858R ctDNA, activated split-crRNA Cas12a (SCas12a) cleaved the loop region of a cascade hairpin probe, resulting in the release of functional spacer RNA (sRNA) molecules. The liberated sRNA further activated additional SCas12a complexes in the presence of assistant DNA, thereby establishing a positive-feedback autocatalytic nucleic acid circuit for exponential-like signal amplification. Simultaneously, a phosphorothioate-modified G-quadruplex hairpin probe was introduced as a low-background "signal-on" fluorescence reporter. Activated SCas12a continuously cleaved the loop region of the probe, releasing phosphorothioate-modified G-quadruplex that subsequently bound Thioflavin T to generate strong fluorescence signals. Benefiting from the synergistic integration of autocatalytic amplification and low-background signals, AutoSCas achieved ultrasensitive and highly specific ctDNA detection with a detection limit as low as 2 aM. Therefore, AutoSCas platform provides a pre-amplification-free strategy for highly sensitive SNV analysis and expands the design of split-crRNA-based CRISPR sensing systems.
